forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Treasury Management Monitoring Report Q1 2026-27
findings.headline: Statutory override on pooled fund accounting extended to April 2029, addressing contingency that prompted £5m reserve setup
findings.detail: The Government has extended the statutory override allowing councils to spread gains and losses on pooled investment funds over multiple years rather than recognizing them immediately. The extension runs until 1 April 2029 for investments in place before 1 April 2024. The MCA had set up a £5m reserve to mitigate the impact if the override had not been extended; that contingency has now been addressed.
findings.matters: The accounting treatment of unrealised investment losses affects financial reporting and the contingency reserves authorities must hold; the extension removes an immediate risk to usable reserves and reduces contingency planning burden.
findings.figures: £5m reserve had been set aside; statutory override extended to 1 April 2029
findings.quote: The statutory override will be extended up until the 1st April 2029 for investments already in place before 1st April 2024. The MCA had set up a reserve of £5m to mitigate the impact of the statutory override not being extended.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Treasury Management Monitoring Report Q1 2026-27
findings.headline: Mayoral Combined Authority holds no loans and has no underlying need to borrow for capital expenditure
findings.detail: As at 31 July 2026, the MCA held no loans outstanding. The authority has no underlying need to borrow long-term to fund capital expenditure. Short-term borrowing may be used only to cover unplanned cash flow shortages as they arise.
findings.matters: Many councils are dependent on borrowing for capital schemes; this authority's position indicates strong cash management and capital position. Lenders assess debt dependency as a key credit risk indicator.
findings.figures: £0m loans outstanding as at 31 July 2026; £450.2m invested funds available
findings.quote: The Mayoral Combined Authority does not currently have any underlying need to borrow long term to fund capital expenditure. As at 31st July 2026 the Mayoral Combined Authority held no loans.

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Treasury Management Monitoring Report Q1 2026-27
findings.headline: Strategic pooled funds holding £49.1m show £2.8m unrealised capital loss but generate 4.5% annual return supporting services
findings.detail: The MCA holds £49.1m in externally managed strategic pooled funds showing £2.8m of unrealised capital loss at fair value (down from purchase value of £51.956m). These funds are generating an average total return of 4.5%, which is used to support services in-year, with cumulative income return since purchase of £11.384m.
findings.matters: Finance directors need to understand mark-to-market exposure in investment portfolios, particularly where unrealised losses exist; indicates portfolio volatility from recent market shocks including the Iran war and energy price spikes.
findings.figures: £2.8m unrealised loss on £49.1m invested (5.4% loss); 4.5% average annual return; £11.384m income return since purchase
findings.quote: These funds are generating an average total return of 4.5% which is used to support services in year, and £2.8m of unrealised capital loss

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.paper_title: Item 10 - Treasury Management Monitoring Report Q1 2026-27
findings.headline: Full-year investment income forecast at £16.7m against budget of £16.1m, a positive variance of £0.6m
findings.detail: The MCA expects to achieve a forecast year-end outturn of £16.7m for investment income against a full-year budget of £16.1m, representing a positive variance of £0.6m (3.7%). The report states this results from the Mayoral Combined Authority's successful treasury strategy and investment decisions.
findings.matters: Investment income is a key source of funding for services; outperformance of this scale indicates competent cash and investment management and provides additional resources.
findings.figures: £16.7m forecast vs £16.1m budget = £0.6m variance; portfolio average return 4.3%
findings.quote: The full year budget for 2026-27 investment income is £16.1m and following the Mayoral Combined Authority's successful treasury strategy and investment decisions, will expect to achieve a forecast year end outturn position of £16.7m which is a positive variance of £0.6m

findings.committee: West of England Combined Authority Audit Committee
findings.headline: Internal control framework assessed as satisfactory with no significant policy breaches or systemic fraud failures in 2025/26
findings.detail: The Head of Audit & Assurance assessed the 2025/26 internal control framework as satisfactory, consistent with the prior year. No significant breaches of financial regulations or contract standing orders were identified, no systemic fraud failures occurred, and no fundamental control breakdowns affected business-critical functions.
findings.matters: Overall control environment assessment is the baseline indicator of governance quality and fraud risk; satisfactory rating provides assurance that internal controls remain adequate
findings.figures: 96% of prior year audit recommendations implemented (65 of 68); no fraud incidents or whistleblowing submissions in 2025/26
findings.quote: we are reporting the state of the internal control framework as satisfactory based on our audit opinions and delivery of the 2025/26 Annual Internal Audit Plan.
